 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Golden State Warriors will likely play an extended period without their best player and veteran superstar Stephen Curry after he exited their recent game against the Houston Rockets early after getting tangled up with Alperen Sengun .
 Although Stephen Curry initiated contact with Alperen Sengun, many NBA fans on social media blamed the Rockets' 'dirty' tactics against the Warriors' superstar for his injury.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, instead of piling on as you would expect, the Warriors' veteran Draymond Green defended the Rockets against these accusations. He argued that while their style is physical, especially on Stephen Curry, and he even accuses them of flopping sometimes, he wouldn't call them a dirty team.
 "I know a lot of people are saying, 'Oh, man, the Houston Rockets are a dirty team.' I don't get into the whole 'dirty' thing. Every now and then, you see some people who do things that are downright dirty. When it happens, I'll speak on it," the Warriors veteran said on the 'Draymond Green Show.'
 "Do they do some b——t when we play them? Absolutely. I think the thing that may irritate me the most is that they play super physically, but then they start flopping sometimes. I would say that irritates me more, but I'm not going to sit here and call them a dirty team," Green said.
 "They're a physical team. And by the way, when we were watching film before the game, you could see it. They're physical as hell. So, give them credit. I'm not going to sit here and call them a dirty team. I'm definitely not going to do that." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "But, having said that, they are a very, very physical team," Green added.
 Multiple incidents in the past, like Dillon Brooks intentionally targeting Curry's injured hand in the 2024-25 playoffs , naturally make a well-aware spectator question Ime Udoka's and the Rockets' defensive strategies. But Green believes the Rockets were not to blame this time.
 Additionally, Green also reflected on how the Warriors plan to deal with Stephen Curry's absence for at least the next three weeks.
 "As we move forward now, with at least three weeks without Steph, and then we'll probably re-evaluate from there, we're going to need guys to step up. I'll probably have to shoot more. No ifs, ands, or buts about it." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We're going to need Yax to step up. It's a lot to ask of a rookie, but I think what we've seen is that this rookie is cut out for it. BP is going to have to step up, too. By the way, both of those guys have been playing incredibly. Both of them have been stepping up." 
 "But the one thing we've talked about with this team is our depth, and we're going to need guys to step up. Mel is going to need to step up." 
 "As I said before, with B-Will out, you look at it and see that he's averaging almost 11 points in 14 or 15 minutes per game. That speed burst, that ability to break down a defense, get into the teeth of the defense, finish or kick out, and create shots for others; we're going to miss that," Green said.
 "Like I said, especially with Steph out, it would have been ideal to have B-Will healthy right now. But we don't, and that is what it is. You have to roll with the punches and figure it out." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think this team, as I said last night, is better equipped to figure it out and be a much better team without Steph this year. I'm not saying we can just go on without Steph. That's not what I'm saying. But to try to hold the fort down while he's out, I think this team is a little better equipped than we were a year ago," Draymond Green concluded.
 Stephen Curry was averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists, and 3.7 rebounds while shooting 50.0% from the field and 45.7% from behind the three-point line before his injury. His averages fell below 30.0 points per game only because they include the three-point night he had against the Rockets.
 While Draymond Green has refused to label the Rockets dirty, his biggest concern now is helping the Warriors survive Curry's absence.
 The next three weeks will test the Warriors' depth, with Yaxel Lendeborg , Brandin Podziemski , and Green expected to shoulder more responsibility as the team tries to stay competitive.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Warriors have fallen to 8-4 for the season after the Rockets snapped their eight-game winning streak in the 108-115 loss . It remains to be seen whether they can maintain their stellar form in Stephen Curry's absence as they face the Spurs tonight at San Antonio's Frost Bank Center.
